subject: trekkies
one_liner: A PC game store for Star Trek fans who take time off work to finish a starship's paperwork.
brand_voice_notes: Shoreleave is a fictional product from the worst AI studio ever. Treat the customer's commitment as entirely reasonable. Explain the game-store mechanics in ordinary language, then let purchase records, printed instructions and holiday requests expose the consequences. Functional labels stay plain. Prices buy fictional games and expansions once; they are not subscriptions. Use original ships, characters and insignia without suggesting an official Star Trek or Steam affiliation.
demo_screen_concept: One game-store detail screen for Captain's Chair. A large starship-bridge screenshot sits beside a purchase panel with three edition choices. Selecting Standard, Command or Fleet updates the price, included ships and outstanding crew holiday requests: $19 and 430, $34 and 860, or $59 and 2,150. Add to cart produces an inline cart summary with the selected edition and matching total. Below the screenshot, tabs reveal Achievements, Community mods and Reviews without leaving the screen. Achievements shows 99 of 100 completed, with Approve all crew leave remaining. Community mods offers a menu-translation preview: switch it on to replace the screenshot's live menu labels with invented alien lettering; Show English opens the reference sheet that now covers part of the planet outside. Reviews shows a Not recommended verdict, 286 hours played and a club reply saying six members have bought copies. Keep prices, counts, labels and review text live and readable. On narrow screens, stack screenshot, purchase panel and detail tabs in that order.

hero.h1: You took a day off to approve everyone else's.
hero.sub: Shoreleave is a PC game store for Star Trek fans. Buy a starship simulator, chase every achievement and spend Friday processing 430 crew holiday requests.

features.title: Finish every achievement.
features.blurb: You've discovered six planets and negotiated a peace treaty. The last achievement requires approving all 430 crew holiday requests. Take Friday off your payroll job to finish them. Every member of the crew will have a proper break.

features.title: Install community mods.
features.blurb: Replace the menus with your favourite alien alphabet using a community mod. The bridge finally looks authentic. Tape an English printout over part of the viewscreen so you can find Quit.

features.title: Publish your review.
features.blurb: Explain why the captain's decision ruined the game. Your Not recommended review appears beside 286 hours played. Six club members buy it to see what upset you, then ask you to host the weekly session.

observations.behavior: Completionists will keep doing an activity they dislike to remove the final unfinished item.
observations.mechanic: A game library tracks achievements and exposes one remaining task: approving every crew member's holiday request.
observations.consequence: A payroll administrator uses real annual leave to perform fictional personnel administration, securing a holiday for everyone except herself.

observations.behavior: Fans pursue authenticity as evidence that they belong, even when the authentic version is harder to use.
observations.mechanic: A community workshop distributes a mod that replaces familiar menu labels with an alien alphabet.
observations.consequence: The convincing starship interface requires a printed English instruction sheet taped over the view of space. The captain brings laminated appliance instructions to game night.

observations.behavior: Disappointed fans want others to understand precisely why something they keep consuming has let them down.
observations.mechanic: A public negative review displays the owner's recorded playtime and appears on the same page as the purchase controls.
observations.consequence: The detailed denunciation sells six copies to curious friends. Its author becomes the regular host of the game he wanted them to reject.

source_product_patterns: A PC game storefront with illustrated game listings and individual purchase prices
A game-detail page combining screenshots, description, review summary and purchase options
Base games and expansion bundles sold as progressively larger editions
An owned-game library with playtime and achievement progress
Community workshop listings for player-made modifications
Public recommended or not-recommended reviews accompanied by hours played
An edition selector and cart summary that preserve the selected purchase
editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: Choose an edition, opening the Captain's Chair store demo. Recognizable product visual: a game-detail page with a broad screenshot gallery, adjacent purchase panel, user-review summary and achievement progress. Opening hierarchy: compact Shoreleave identity and the worst AI studio ever credit, headline, short explanation and CTA, followed immediately by the wide store preview. Make 99/100 achievements and 430 pending holiday requests visible together. Below it, use three feature passages with their relevant interface evidence, then customer accounts and a joined edition comparison. Proposed artwork one is an original in-game bridge scene with an empty captain's chair, a bright planet outside and a personnel terminal in the foreground; it supplies the store screenshot and establishes the glamorous setting occupied by administrative work. The holiday-request interface remains live text over the terminal area. Proposed artwork two is a domestic gaming setup with an English reference sheet physically taped across part of the monitor; it demonstrates the cost of alien-language authenticity. Keep its menu labels and explanatory caption outside the image as readable text. The review needs live text and recorded hours rather than another illustration. On mobile, put the complete product preview directly after the CTA and stack its screenshot above the purchase panel. Digest comparison: the mechanisms are achievement completion becoming unpaid office work, authenticity defeating usability and a negative review recruiting customers. Once-only game editions escalate crew obligations. Testimonials recount a sacrificed holiday, laminated instructions and an unwanted hosting commitment.

references.reference: The bridge consoles in Star Trek: The Next Generation
references.cues: Dark control surfaces, broad rounded color bands, apricot and lavender accents, compact information groups and generous black gaps.
references.application: Use dark plum store panels with apricot primary actions and lavender selection states. Rounded bands organize screenshots, purchase information and progress. Develop original shapes and lettering without reproducing a canonical console or insignia.

references.reference: Star Trek: The Next Generation Technical Manual
references.cues: Pale technical pages, carefully captioned diagrams, condensed headings, numbered references and disciplined alignment.
references.application: Give the landing page a warm off-white manual surface, Barlow Condensed headings and Source Sans 3 body text. Number feature evidence and align captions with their images. Present the English menu reference as a practical diagram sheet.

audience_design.landing_application: Combine the manual's pale pages with inset bridge-console product panels. Use warm off-white #F3EFE6, dark plum #252133, apricot #E5A16C and muted lavender #B5A0D8. Barlow Condensed supplies compact display headings; Source Sans 3 handles explanations, prices and controls. Original game screenshots provide the main imagery, with the domestic reference-sheet photograph supporting the second feature. Use a broad opening store preview, clear horizontal section divisions and an aligned edition table. Keep body text in ordinary sentence case and reserve numbering for useful references.
audience_design.demo_application: Increase information density inside the same plum, apricot and lavender system. Preserve the game store's screenshot gallery, purchase sidebar, edition selector, achievement progress, community-mod listing and playtime-bearing reviews. Use readable rectangular controls inside the larger rounded panel groups. The audience references affect typography, color and framing while the store workflow remains easy to recognize. Keep the English reference control legible when the fictional menu translation is active.

design_direction.style: Retro-futurist technical manual: pale captioned pages with dark plum bridge-console insets and broad interrupted rounded bands.

palette.name: Manual Paper, Bridge Plum, Apricot and Lavender

fonts.pairing: Bundled Sports/Fitness Barlow Condensed display combined with Corporate Trust Source Sans 3 body; preserves both host-approved fonts.

design_direction.archetype: PC game storefront landing with a broad screenshot-and-purchase preview, manual-style feature evidence, composed graphic spreads, player accounts and joined edition comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 150ms color feedback and deliberate tab or selection state changes; no ambient animation. Reduced-motion removes transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Large two-line-capable manual heading beside compact subcopy and primary action; immediately below, a full-width game screenshot and edition purchase panel. Live 99/100 achievements and 430 crew holiday requests. On mobile stack proposition, screenshot, purchase panel; keep every request count and price readable.
design_direction.design_review: All seven supplied digest identities compared. No matching style/palette/fonts tuple. Interrupted command bands and an empty captain chair differ from prize rosettes, train sidings, yearbook cursor, cabinets, salvage tags, album sleeves and pond contours. Retain library preview/content hierarchy and accessible UI rules; reject generic vibrant community blocks, neon purple and Exo/Roboto Mono because the approved manual/bridge references are authoritative.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: An empty captain chair makes the customer absence visible. Its broad console arms and a leave-ticket notch bridge heroic command and office leave. A bespoke narrow Shoreleave wordmark joins technical-manual typography with console curves. Artwork uses printed technical collage, not the previous entries' documentary catalogues or mascots.

logo.concept: Selected Gemini direction A: an empty apricot command chair, lavender rounded console arms and dark plum base with bespoke correctly spelled Shoreleave lettering. Stronger at nav and icon sizes than B, whose interrupted doorway reads as a generic control badge. Wordmark spelling, kerning and silhouette visually inspected.
logo.clear_space: At least half the symbol height on every side; faithful exports preserve a paper surround.
logo.placement: Landing navigation and footer, demo chrome; faithful symbol crop as favicon on both pages.

items.prompt: Original identity design for Shoreleave, a fictional PC game store for adult Star Trek fans who use real holidays to approve fictional crew holidays. Original identity only: no Star Trek delta, official insignia, Steam logo, stock gaming badge, stars, orbit or gradient. Warm paper #F3EFE6 flat opaque background, dark plum #252133, apricot #E5A16C, lavender #B5A0D8. Finish an actual clean standalone horizontal logo, NOT a brand board or mockup. Exact single word Shoreleave, spelled S h o r e l e a v e, capital S only. Broad custom narrow humanist lettering with subtle rounded console corners, impeccable kerning. Symbol on left, wordmark on right, generous clear space, fill middle 85 percent of width. No other words, no small captions, no shadows or texture. DIRECTION A: design a memorable minimal EMPTY CAPTAIN CHAIR viewed straight on: one apricot high back and seat, two broad lavender rounded console armrests, dark plum base, negative-space separation. Its silhouette must be legible at 24px. The chair is unattended because its captain is processing holiday forms. Give the wordmark a confident technical-manual voice.
items.placement: Landing navigation and footer; demo header
items.verdict: Accepted direction A. Correct spelling, open counters and recognizable empty chair. Faithfully trimmed paper surround; no artwork redrawn.

items.prompt: Create one cinematic high-quality 3D PC GAME ENVIRONMENT STILL, original science-fiction starship bridge for Captain's Chair, fictional game sold by Shoreleave. Attached image is APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE for empty chair design and palette, not an image to paste. Adult 1990s television science-fiction fan aesthetic: dark plum #252133 hull and console surfaces, lavender #B5A0D8 padded arms, apricot #E5A16C chair upholstery, warm off-white trim. Wide symmetrical perspective from rear of bridge, one unmistakable EMPTY captain chair in middle foreground, sweeping ergonomic consoles, extraordinary huge warm apricot planet and moon through wide front windows, lavender atmospheric light, carefully modeled mechanical materials, gorgeous playable-game environment rather than real photography. Left foreground has a simple dark personnel terminal angled toward viewer, with BLANK dark display to allow live HTML controls later. No people, no lettering, NO TEXT, no logos, no insignia, no numbers, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens, no game HUD. No recognizable franchise-specific ship or canonical bridge, invent architecture and furniture. Keep planet visible above chair; bright detailed scene in 16:9.
items.placement: Opening storefront preview and demo screenshot gallery
items.verdict: Accepted. Empty chair matches identity; original bridge, bright planet, blank foreground terminal, no labels or insignia. Main product context clear.

items.prompt: Create an editorial documentary photograph of a real domestic PC gaming desk in a modest British spare room at evening. Attached first image is APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE for the apricot/lavender/plum design language, NOT a logo to paste. A computer monitor shows only an original 3D science-fiction bridge environment with an EMPTY APRICOT captain chair and a large orange planet, no interface, no typography. A large plain white reference page, with NO WRITING OR PRINT whatsoever, is taped across the RIGHT THIRD of the screen with two pieces of masking tape, physically hiding part of the planet. Nearby keyboard, ceramic tea mug, practical home desk and an unbranded laminating pouch. Tactile, believable slightly mundane office-photo composition, monitor dominates. No people, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI controls, no icons, no words on any surface. Landscape 4:3. The gag is clearly a beautiful view of space partly blocked by a piece of domestic office paper. Natural photography, not diagram, not illustration.
items.placement: Landing player accounts beside English reference sheet
items.verdict: Accepted. Believable home desk; blank paper visibly obstructs planet. English reference labels supplied as live HTML on paper. No essential text baked into photo.
